claims.claim: Analysis of more than 17,000 U.S. men found higher ultra-processed food intake corresponded to 24-31 percent elevated prostate cancer incidence after adjustment for age, smoking, race, and poverty status.
claims.episode_span: Analysis of more than 17,000 U.S. men found that higher consumption of soft drinks, packaged snacks, and processed meats corresponded to 24–31 percent elevated prostate cancer incidence after adjustment for age, smoking, and socioeconomic factors.
claims.source_title: Eating more ultra-processed foods may raise prostate cancer risk by 30%
claims.supporting_quote: those who ate more ultra-processed foods, including soft drinks, packaged snacks, cereals, and processed meats, had roughly 24% to 31% higher risks of prostate cancer after accounting for factors such as age, smoking, race and ethnicity, and poverty status.
